citation: Hayabuchi H, Morita R, Ohta M, Nanri A, et al. Validation of preferred salt concentration in soup based on a randomized blinded experiment in multiple regions in Japan - influence of umami (L-glutamate) on saltiness and palatability of low-salt solutions. Hypertens Res. 2020.
matrix: water (distilled water; NaCl with or without MSG)
panel: 584 healthy adults from 19 regions of Japan, untrained (consumer)
scale: 100-mm VAS (left: not at all salty; right: extremely salty); mean of two evaluations
location: Table 2, row 'All' (N = 584); Table 4 for sodium content; Results text
quote: saltiness of the 0.3% NaCl solution with MSG was significantly higher than that of the 0.3% NaCl without MSG (39.1
notes: Conversions: % taken as g/100 mL (Table 4 header gives NaCl in g/100 mL), so 0.3% = 3 g/L, 0.6% = 6 g/L, 0.9% = 9 g/L; MSG 0.3% = 3 g/L. MSG hydrate form not stated; Table 4 gives Na of 0.118 vs 0.155 g/100 mL for 0.3% NaCl without/with MSG, i.e. 0.037 g Na from 0.3 g MSG, which matches the monohydrate (0.3 x 22.99/187.13 = 0.0369) better than anhydrous (0.3 x 22.99/169.11 = 0.0408): my inference, not a statement in the paper. Only saltiness and palatability were rated; umami was not rated. Sites recorded water temperature but no value was found in the text read. Subgroup rows (sex, age) are also in Table 2. This is a salt x umami study: it tests whether MSG changes saltiness. Morita et al. 2021 (PMC7916089) reanalyses what appears to be the same experiment (561 participants; 'All' row 23.51, 39.28, 55.81, 58.24, 73.76, 72.42), so it is not entered as a separate study.

notes: Conversion: salt % w/v x 10 = g/L (0.35% = 3.5 g/L). NaCl_g_per_L is the ADDED salt only. Table 5 of the paper has 16 seasoned chicken soups (salty and umami scores) but the stock (chicken bones, soy sauce, sugar, radish) was not analysed, so those are not entered. notes: Conversion: % x 10 = g/L, treating % as w/v (the paper only says '%'; w/v or w/w is not stated): sucrose 2% = 20 g/L, citric acid 0.008% = 0.08 g/L. Citric acid levels are very low (0.06 to 1.92 g/L, sourness series only 0.08 to 0.24 g/L) yet reach Imax 11.13, see the 'looked wrong' list.
